class_name: 授受-内の受益-テモラウ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1: author → mechanical attachment gate → cold review → fixes applied → gate re-run

patterns.usage_note: The receiver is the subject, so the event is framed as a benefit obtained, very often one the receiver arranged or asked for; てくれる (1271) reports the same favor with the giver as subject. The person who acts is marked with に (から is also possible when something is handed over or told). Unlike てくれる, the beneficiary here need not be the speaker: 弟は先輩に直してもらった is fine. The humble counterpart is ていただく (1301).

examples.ruby: 兄[あに]に自転車[じてんしゃ]のパンクを直[なお]してもらった。
examples.english: I had my older brother fix the flat on my bike.

examples.ruby: 早[はや]めに医者[いしゃ]に傷[きず]を見[み]てもらうつもりだ。
examples.english: I mean to get a doctor to look at the cut before long.

examples.ruby: 駅前[えきまえ]の店[みせ]で時計[とけい]の電池[でんち]を交換[こうかん]してもらった。
examples.english: I had the shop by the station swap the battery in my watch.

patterns.usage_note: The humble (謙譲語) counterpart of てもらう, used when the person doing the favor outranks you; 〜ていただけますか / 〜ていただけませんか are the standard way to phrase a business request. Keep one perspective per sentence: ていただく puts you, the receiver, in the subject slot, while てくださる (1281) keeps the other person there. 頂く and 戴く are the kanji spellings, but the auxiliary is usually written in kana.

examples.ruby: 先生[せんせい]に卒業論文[そつぎょうろんぶん]を読[よ]んでいただいた。
examples.english: I was fortunate enough to have my professor read my thesis.

examples.ruby: 来週[らいしゅう]、部長[ぶちょう]に空港[くうこう]まで送[おく]っていただきます。
examples.english: Next week the department head will be good enough to drive me to the airport.

examples.ruby: 近所[きんじょ]の方[かた]に留守中[るすちゅう]の郵便[ゆうびん]を預[あず]かっていただいた。
examples.english: A neighbor was kind enough to hold my mail while I was away.
